concurrency_model.kernel: core/src/semantic/concurrency.rs: ConcurrencyKind (Await, Spawn real; Lock/Unlock/ChannelCreate/ChannelSend/ChannelReceive/AtomicOp declared, never emitted), ConcurrencyIdentity { repository, revision, function, kind, span }.
concurrency_model.scope_this_wave: `expr.await` is dedicated syn::Expr::Await syntax, cannot be shadowed or overloaded -> Await, always Observed. A call whose callee spelling ends in the segment `spawn` -> Spawn, recorded as Inferred (corrected this pass from Observed): a locally-defined `fn spawn()` or an unrelated `game::spawn(enemy)` is not evidence of real concurrency, and this extractor has no call-target resolution to tell the two apart. Lock/Unlock/channel/atomic operations are declared but never emitted -- method names like `.lock()`/`.send()`/`.recv()` collide constantly with unrelated user-defined methods, and claiming them from a bare method name alone would fabricate compiler-resolved semantics.
